definitions.explanation: Physical or emotional distress. The noun form of the verb 苦しむ (to suffer). Covers a wide range from physical pain to deep emotional torment.

examples.japanese: {苦|くる}しみから{逃|に}げたい。
examples.english: I want to escape from the suffering.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{苦|くる}しみは{誰|だれ}にもわからない。
{長|なが}い{病気|びょうき}の{苦|くる}しみを{乗|の}り{越|こ}えて、やっと{元気|げんき}になった。
examples.english: After overcoming the suffering of a long illness, I finally got well.

notes:
USAGE:
{苦|くる}しみ is the nominal form of {苦|くる}しむ (to suffer). It conveys deeper, more prolonged distress than {痛|いた}み (pain), which is primarily physical. {苦|くる}しみ encompasses both physical and emotional suffering.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦|くる}しみを{味|あじ}わう: to experience suffering
- {苦|くる}しみに{耐|た}える: to endure suffering
- {苦|くる}しみから{逃|に}れる: to escape from suffering
- {苦|くる}しみを{乗|の}り{越|こ}える: to overcome suffering
- {苦|くる}しみを{分|わ}かち{合|あ}う: to share suffering
